speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong and I will address earlier Parliamentary Question Nos 2 to 14 and Question Nos 15 to 18 for Questions for Written Answer from today's Order Paper, as well as questions filed by Members of Parliament for future Sittings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We strengthened our healthcare system, enhanced our contact tracing capability, expanded our testing capacity and introduced safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All these efforts work together as a multi-layered defence system to keep us safe from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With the continued support and sacrifices of everyone in Singapore, we have brought the situation under control and kept community transmissions low.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have now moved into Phase Three and are making steady progress towards a new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, this is not the moment to be complacent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Globally, daily infection numbers and deaths continue to rise in many countries, constantly setting new records, including countries that had been successful in containing their outbreaks previously.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also seen the emergence of new variants that appear to be more transmissible and have had to tighten some of our border restrictions as a precaution.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must, therefore, be prepared that, despite best efforts, new infections will still occur here from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We face the continuing risk of new clusters and outbreaks and the danger of a new wave of infections getting out of control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be the new normal for a long time to come.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That is why we still need to keep up our multi-layered defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In fact, we must further strengthen it as we continue our journey through Phase Three.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Vaccination is a new line of defence we must put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Vaccination is a critical shield to protect us and our loved ones against COVID-19 even as the global situation remains volatile.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will also be a key enabler, allowing us to return to normalcy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Expert Committee on COVID-19 Vaccination – comprising professionals in infectious diseases, immunology and other relevant fields – has studied the available data on the vaccine, reviewed the reports from the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), deliberated at length and considered carefully safety and efficacy aspects of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It recommended that everyone who is medically eligible should be vaccinated so that Singapore can achieve as high a level of vaccination coverage as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A high level of vaccination coverage will maximise protection for the population and minimise the proportion of persons still susceptible to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will, in turn, reduce the risk of large outbreaks and continue to keep community cases low and allow us to further reopen the economy and resume more normal, social activities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We received our first shipment of vaccines from Pfizer-BioNTech at the end of last year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our first vaccinations were conducted at the National Centre of Infectious Diseases last week.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is an important milestone and we are beginning to see the light at the end of this very long tunnel.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Louis Chua asked about the number of vaccines that we have secured.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A team headed by the Head of Civil Service led the efforts and undertook this very urgent, complex and difficult task.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The vaccines will arrive in Singapore in batches, given high global demand, especially from countries with high rates of infection.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Pharmaceutical companies will also need time to scale up vaccine production and distribution.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Following the first shipment of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine at the end of last year, we are expecting more deliveries in the next few months, including from Moderna and Sinovac.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As recommended by the Expert Committee, we will prioritise vaccinations of groups that are most at risk.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is also consistent with the World Health Organization's guidance and similar to what other countries are doing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will, therefore, begin with the healthcare workers and staff working in the healthcare sector as they work in direct care of patients or in supporting roles.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also prioritise others who are in jobs or settings where risk of super-spreading events is high, such as the construction, marine and process sectors, including migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Thereafter, we will progressively broaden our vaccinations to include other Singaporeans and long-term residents who are medically eligible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As more vaccines are approved for use, we will adjust our vaccination programme, depending on the vaccine supply as well as the disease epidemiology at that point in time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The national effort to vaccinate the population will require considerable resources to implement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is one of our key focus areas this year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The scale of the current effort is larger but we are also much better prepared.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We started planning for this very early on.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have put in place end-to-end processes to meet the cold-chain logistics requirements – from delivery and receipt at the airport, through to storage and then transport to vaccination sites – so that the quality and efficacy of the vaccines are not compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While our healthcare workers are receiving their vaccinations within their healthcare institutions, we are concurrently readying clinics and vaccination centres for others to be vaccinated when it is their turn.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Prior bookings will be necessary, given the cold-chain requirements at the vaccination sites and multi-dose vials of the vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It will also ensure operational efficiency and minimise individual wait times.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: More information on how to make the booking will be provided later.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, we will test our systems thoroughly before ramping up to ensure that vaccination operations proceed smoothly and patient safety is not compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There were several questions from Members, including Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Sylvia Lim, on the safety and efficacy of the vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These concerns are understandable, given the extraordinary speed at which the COVID-19 vaccines have been developed and brought to the market.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The speed achieved is the result of a strong and concerted global response to a major pandemic rather than a compromise of safety standards.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First of all, the vaccine must be approved by HSA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These standards are the same as those used for full vaccine evaluations except that long-term data from clinical trials will only be evaluated later as the data becomes available.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The data that has been reviewed includes those from pre-clinical studies done in laboratories, clinical trials on human volunteers, manufacturing and quality controls as well as the on-going experience with the actual use of the vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The assessment and recommendations for the vaccines are also reviewed by HSA's Medicines Advisory Committee and Panel of Infectious Diseases Experts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HSA will only allow a COVID-19 vaccine to be used if it is assessed to be sufficiently efficacious and safe for use and only if the benefits of the vaccine are assessed to outweigh the risks of any potential adverse effects from the vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Moderna and Sinovac vaccines are also currently undergoing the review process.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Following HSA's approval, the independent Expert Committee appointed by MOH has also reviewed the clinical data on the safety and efficacy of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine and has been briefed by HSA on the full range of considerations in granting interim authorisation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Expert Committee concurs with HSA – that the vaccine is suitable for use in Singapore, for persons aged 16 years and above, for the prevention of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In assessing the suitability of vaccine candidates for specific population groups, the Expert Committee took into consideration four key criteria – vaccine safety, vaccine efficacy, vaccine tolerability and data adequacy of clinical trials.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether there is any data to show that the current COVID-19 vaccines are effective against the new strain seen in the UK and Europe.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mutations occur in viruses naturally and different strains can emerge from time to time, especially in a long-drawn pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While this B.1.1.7 strain from UK does appear to be more transmissible, there is currently no evidence that current COVID-19 vaccines are less effective against this strain.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Experts have said that it is unlikely that mutations would impact effectiveness of current vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Vaccine producers such as Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna have also come forward to reassure that their vaccines should protect against the B.1.1.7 variant, and are undertaking studies to formally confirm this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH will evaluate the data as it emerges and review our vaccine strategy and border measures, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and others have asked about potential side effects.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Both HSA and the Expert Committee have studied the data, from clinical trials as well as actual experience from vaccinations carried out in other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They have factored this into their evaluation before granting authorisation or making a recommendation on the use of COVID-19 vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Based on data available today, people who receive the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine may experience side effects such as pain in the injection site, fatigue, fever, muscle aches, or headaches.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These are similar to side effects for other established vaccines and they usually resolve on their own in a few days.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As with all medications and established vaccines, there is a small risk of very rare but serious adverse events that may occur post-vaccination, including allergic reactions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we expect few to need this, the programme will give a greater peace of mind for those taking the vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Further details on the programme will be provided in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, HSA requires vaccine manufacturers to submit new information continually for active review.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HSA and the Expert Committee will also continue to monitor and review the efficacy and safety of COVID-19 vaccines in the local population and internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This includes data on specific population subgroups such as those below age of 16, persons with immunosuppression, or pregnant women that were excluded from initial clinical trials.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HSA and the Expert Committee will also look at long-term safety data to detect rare and severe adverse events, and study the durability of protection provided by the vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This on-going monitoring is the norm expected for any vaccines that first come into use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked whether there will be a need to separate blood collected from donors who have and have not received COVID-19 vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While the COVID-19 vaccination will be voluntary, we strongly encourage everyone who is medically eligible to get vaccinated when the vaccine is offered to you.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will not only provide protection to yourself, but also indirectly protect those who cannot be vaccinated due to medical reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This collective protection would be more effective the more are vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In turn, we can keep the number of cases low, minimise the stress on our healthcare system, ensure that those who are ill get the treatment that they need and allow us to return to normalcy sooner.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some may feel that there is no urgency to get vaccinated given the current low number of community cases and the local situation is under control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must not be complacent or wait till an outbreak and then rush to be vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have seen a few community cases in the last few days, which shows clearly that there are hidden cases among us.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are also seeing new variants that are more contagious.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Any of these cases has a risk of sparking a major outbreak as we have seen in other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If people wait until an outbreak has happened to get themselves vaccinated, it will be too late – both to protect themselves and to prevent the outbreak in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the Prime Minister has said, we have every confidence in our experts and the process that has been put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Prime Minister and our Cabinet colleagues, including myself, will lead on this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will be getting vaccinated as early as possible when our turn comes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This excludes Short-Term Visit Pass holders, such as tourists.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I understand Mr Yip Hon Weng would like to know whether those who are not vaccinated will have their job scopes reviewed, in order to reduce exposure to the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In most instances, redeployment of non-vaccinated employees is unlikely to be necessary, unless there is a resurgence of local cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But all workers should continue to take the necessary precautions such as mask-wearing, and where required, donning of Personal Protective Equipment or PPE, and undergoing Rostered Routine Testing or RRT.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That said, there may be specific cases such as researchers or laboratory staff working directly on the COVID-19 virus or those who face very high risk of exposure to infected individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH and MOM are reviewing the issue of vaccination of workers in such workplace settings and will provide further advice later.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har asked if individuals will be issued vaccination cards after receiving the COVID-19 vaccination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, any person who is vaccinated will have their record updated in the National Immunisation Registry, and individuals will be able to check their vaccination status digitally.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked if individuals will be given a choice of vaccines when more than one has been approved for use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Any COVID-19 vaccine that is approved for use will have to meet the stringent safety and efficacy requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, it is not necessary to allow individuals to have choice of vaccines, which will unnecessarily complicate the already complex vaccination programme.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Anyway, in the immediate term, only the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine has been approved for use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Alex Yam and Ms He Ting Ru asked about our public communications strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Government agencies have been using various channels to understand public sentiments on the COVID-19 vaccines, including ground outreach and surveys.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue our efforts to reach out to our population to explain the importance of vaccination and to assure them of the safety and efficacy of the vaccines we are using.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I hope parliamentary colleagues will also help to share the information with your constituents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I would also like to urge everyone to refer to official or credible sources of information and not to forward unconfirmed or untrue information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Investigations revealed that there was no causal relationship between the vaccine and the two individuals’ deaths.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Spreading such misinformation undermines our efforts to protect Singapore and Singaporeans against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have come a long way in the past year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many have missed their vacations for the whole year.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have had to learn and manage with safe distancing measures when we are out and about.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is only through everyone’s concerted efforts that local transmission is now low in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, the global situation is still far from under control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Every vaccine will meet all our safety and efficacy requirements before being approved for use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And I strongly encourage all Singaporeans and long-term residents to get vaccinated when the vaccine is offered to you, to protect yourselves and your loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be the key focus of the MTF over the next few months.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Let us all do our part, so we can overcome and emerge stronger together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Minister for Education will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on both Statements after this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister Gan has just given an update on our vaccination plans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have worked hard together over the past year to get to where we are today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have put in place some very tough measures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a crisis like this, we have learnt to expect the unpredictable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But new issues will inevitably crop up and some things will go wrong.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a careful acknowledgement of our state of readiness to resume more activities in a controlled manner.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The specific adjustments from Phase Two to Phase Three may not seem like a lot.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, in his Parliamentary Question (PQ), Mr Leong Mun Wai said there’s “little change”.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But let us not trivialise these hard-won gains.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are the result of the efforts and sacrifices by many people over the course of the year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, we are not out of the woods yet.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot afford to relax and let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Minister Gan highlighted just now, the global situation continues to escalate rapidly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Cases continue to climb in many countries, including in places which had previously established good control over the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In Singapore, in recent days we have already seen two family clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Marine workers went on board ships, they got infected and they spread the virus to their family members, including their spouses and children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One of the children had a school-mate who visited the home and was infected.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fortunately, this happened during the school holidays, so they had limited contact with other students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is a sobering reminder of how easily new infection clusters can break out. it only takes one super spreader event to spark another major outbreak, so we must continue to stay alert and vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The emergence of new viral strains that may be more infectious, such as the B.1.1.7 variant, is indeed very worrying.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I share the concerns raised by Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Melvin Yong.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where necessary and practical, we will tighten our border restrictions to limit importation risk.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also recently tightened the testing regime and safe management measures for those working in the aviation and maritime sectors, as they are the ones who are most likely to be interfacing with travellers and crew from overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, for air crew who have layovers in higher risk countries, we are testing them more frequently after they return to Singapore and requiring them to self-isolate for a few days.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are testing them every seven days instead of 14 days.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not the first time we have picked up new strains of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fact is that the virus has always been mutating, and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not know what their cumulative effects will be like.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will have to constantly monitor the latest developments around the world, review the data and evidence, and update our measures accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the virus raging around the world, we clearly cannot afford to freely open our borders at this time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But neither can we close ourselves completely from the world and simply stop all flights or ships coming to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is an existential issue for us because we do not have the luxury of a hinterland to depend on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Therefore, we take a calculated risk-based approach in managing our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung recently made a Ministerial Statement on this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I will just reiterate the key points.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To facilitate essential business and official travel, we have established special travel arrangements with certain countries and territories.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We control the number of travellers on these schemes tightly, and we require the travellers to stick to a controlled itinerary and strictly limit interactions with the wider community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have a Fast Lane between Singapore and six provinces and municipalities in China, established in June last year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked how many have taken this up.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since early November, we have also allowed short-term Chinese visitors to enter Singapore via the Air Travel Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In order to promote both Singapore’s economic interests and our status as a global business and transportation hub, we will continue to negotiate and formulate additional travel arrangements with other like-minded countries or regions while ensuring that public health is not compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As it would not be practical for these travellers to serve a 14-day quarantine, we manage the risk by placing a “bubble wrap” around these travellers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the travellers will only stay at dedicated facilities and will not be allowed into the community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will also undergo regular testing and observe all prevailing safe management measures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides these special travel arrangements, we have, on a daily basis, a far larger number of travellers who are returning Singaporeans, PRs and long-term pass holders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is also a continued flow of new migrant workers coming in, mostly construction workers and foreign domestic helpers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We need them to build our homes and infrastructure, and to support the care-giving needs of our families.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For these returning residents and essential workers, we allow their inflow on a controlled basis, but we require those who are from higher risk countries to serve a 14-day Stay Home Notice or SHN at dedicated facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will be tested at the end of their SHN.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Travellers from countries with new virus variants will serve their SHN at designated hotels to further minimise the risks of spread.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This system ensures that we are able to tightly ring-fence imported cases and minimise the risk of leakage into the community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since 18 November, we have required all non-citizen and non-PR travellers from higher risk countries or regions coming to Singapore to take a pre-departure test within 72 hours prior to their departure.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have not required this of citizens and PRs because we do not want to place additional barriers for them to return home if they have urgent need to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Additionally, as paediatric testing services may not be so easily available in some countries, those aged six and below are also exempted from this pre-departure test.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that our containment measures depend on good management of the hotels which are used as SHN facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We make sure these facilities have strict protocols in place to segregate persons on SHN from all other guests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These include placing them in segregated blocks, wings or floors, clearly demarcating their route of movement and instituting regular cleaning and disinfection regimes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Persons on SHN are not allowed to use common facilities in the hotels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Once there is a confirmed case, comprehensive contact tracing and ring-fencing of contacts, including staff working in SHN facilities, will be done to prevent further transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And any links between confirmed cases from the same facility will be thoroughly investigated.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even with the multiple layers of safeguards, the risk of leaks, though small, remains.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the recent incident at Mandarin Orchard Hotel is a case in point, as Mr Ang Wei Neng highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Based on our preliminary investigations, there had been no breaches in SHN protocols at Mandarin Orchard Hotel.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But investigations suggest that infection protocols can be improved, for example, through better crowd regulation as well as having good ventilation systems to circulate more fresh air.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to work closely with all SHN hotels to ensure that infection prevention protocols are robust.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Monitoring genetic information of the virus in Singapore’s COVID-19 cases has been important in uncovering the Mandarin Orchard Hotel incident and is required to detect any importation of new COVID-19 strains into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Specific to Dr Tan Wu Meng’s question regarding whole-genome sequencing in Singapore, this is an established capability within the National Public Health Laboratory or NPHL.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where possible, whole-genome sequencing can be performed rapidly and directly on clinical samples of COVID-19 positive cases.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, in samples that have low viral loads, it may be necessary for the virus to be cultured before the sequencing can be done.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to assess available and emerging laboratory technologies so we can improve our capabilities and enhance our responses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One important issue is whether we can relax our border measures for persons who are vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As mentioned earlier, the main benefit of the vaccine is that it offers protection to the vaccinated individual.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is likely that the vaccination can also reduce the risk of transmission of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But at present we still do not know the extent of the reduction.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are several on-going studies on the effectiveness of vaccines in reducing transmission risk and we are monitoring these very closely.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for now, we will continue to take a more cautious approach.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, vaccinated travellers will continue to be subjected to prevailing border measures and SHN requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will fine-tune our approach over time, once we have understand the effect of the vaccine better.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, border measures are just one part of our overall system of defence against the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within our community, we must continue to adopt a calibrated approach towards resumption of activities in Phase Three and minimise the risks of any further flare-ups during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The tools for us to do so are not new – we have repeatedly emphasised them throughout the past year, but I think they bear repeating as we begin this new year because memories are short, as we all know.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under Phase Three we can go out in larger groups of eight people.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By all means, use the opportunity to catch up with family members and loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But please do so responsibly and in accordance with prevailing rules and restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, there are a few who persist in pushing their luck and disregarding the rules.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have stepped up checks over the festive period.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Firm enforcement actions have been taken and will continue to do so against any such breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us also not forget some of the basic measures that we have put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All the good practices that we have emphasised and cultivated over the past few months remain very important – wearing a mask, practising good hygiene, washing of hands regularly, not using your hands to touch your face.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remember we talked about all these repeatedly at the start of the outbreak last year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, testing remains important and we are continuing to deploy more tests as widely as possible, so that cases can be detected quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Anyone who sees a doctor with acute respiratory infections or flu-like symptoms will be advised to take a PCR test.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That was how we picked up several of our recent cases.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is very important for anyone who feels unwell to see the doctor immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if the doctor advises you to be tested, please comply with the doctor’s instructions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those engaged in higher risk activities, we are putting them on a rostered routing testing regime or the RRT.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This already applies to workers in the construction, marine and process sectors, as well as to airport and marine workers, and now to staff in the SHN hotels, as I mentioned just now.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the RRT, we undertake special testing operations from time to time to do a sweep around specific areas or groups of individuals, whom we assess to be at higher risk of transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the past few months, we have done such tests amongst staff of nursing homes, hawkers, as well as bus and taxi drivers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This month, we will be testing the students staying in our University hostels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also been stepping up the use of antigen rapid tests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are useful as a pre-event measure for larger scale activities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are also a very good complement to the PCR tests which are more sensitive but take longer to obtain results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The costs of these rapid tests have been coming down.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over time, we can expect more innovative rapid test kits that are cheaper, faster and more convenient to administer.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will enable us to test more extensively and conveniently, to detect positive cases and protect our population more comprehensively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we first deployed testing in a significant way, I know there were concerns amongst certain groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others were worried that there would be a stigma associated with being identified for testing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I hope by now we can all appreciate and understand the reasons why testing is important and necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Frequent and widespread testing is a critical enabler, which we intend to ramp up over the coming months.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must all start getting used to the idea of regular testing being a part of our lives during this pandemic period.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will continue to strengthen our contact tracing capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite our best efforts at safe management measures and testing, we know that cases will still slip through from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we need to be able to quickly identify and trace the contacts, and ring-fence the clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The TraceTogether and SafeEntry Programme has been, and will continue, to be a key part of our contact tracing operations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Before TraceTogether or TT, we had a good contact tracing system but it was manpower intensive.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It worked well for SARS, but not for COVID-19, where the virus spreads much faster, well before the onset of symptoms and even in cases who themselves remain asymptomatic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the past it took two days for us to interview an infected person, establish all of his close contacts and then get in touch with these people and put them on quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, with TT and SafeEntry, we are able to do all this in a matter of hours.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Once we identify the contacts, we test them immediately, at the start of their quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who are positive, we in turn get their TT data to identity their contacts and then, initiate the tracing process.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this way, we try to get ahead of the virus and contain clusters before they get any bigger.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our ability to do all of these is not just because of the TT programme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is fundamentally because of the confidence and trust that Singaporeans have in our system – the way we handle the data, the way they go about doing contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked if the cost is justified.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I have no doubt about the cost-effectiveness of the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, in developing the programme, we remained mindful of the need to ensure value for money.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Mr Dennis Tan had filed a question on whether we could work on a rechargeable version of the TraceTogether tokens.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Doing so would inevitably increase the cost and also the time needed for manufacturing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we have designed the tokens using off-the-shelf components where possible to minimise manufacturing complexity, time and costs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we certainly encourage an even higher take-up.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am one of them because I think that if I have the token with me, I quite likely to lose it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I just use my phone and that works well for me.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we recognise that some people want the tokens and that is why we made them available and distributed them across all the Community Centres or CCs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Given that the TT app was easily available, we had initially not expected such a strong demand for the tokens.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the supply side, there were also some delays in the manufacturing schedule.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As announced previously, we will also be distributing the tokens to school students who have not yet collected them, through the schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, we have what we call TT-only SafeEntry where the SafeEntry checking in/checking out is done either through the app or the token.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will give further information on this once the details and timelines are firmed up, and will provide adequate advance notice to all the affected establishments, so that they can gear up and prepare.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our healthcare workers and frontline officers – contact tracers, safe distancing ambassadors, our swabbers, enforcement officers, immigration and security officers, airport workers, our SHN operators – have all been working hard round the clock.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are also many who have contributed; many unsung heroes all over Singapore doing their part.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Toward the end of last year, Minister Gan and I held a simple appreciation event – in accordance with all safe distancing rules, of course – to thank the people involved in setting up the COVID-19 Community Care Facility.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is at the Expo and Big Box.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members will recall this was a pivotal moment in our fight against the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The team came together from both the public and private sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the spirit of SG United, they got the facility up and running in a matter of days.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, we have stood down the facilities at the Expo and Big Box because we do not need them for now.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I told the team we will do our best to avoid calling on them again.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I think they were quite relieved to hear that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I was also very heartened when they said, "Don't worry, if the need arises, we will be ready to respond anytime".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the indomitable spirit that gives me confidence in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must not allow this prolonged vigilance to wear us down.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must not falter; we must not weaken or tire.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us approach the new year with the same spirit of fortitude, solidarity and unity that we had shown over the past year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us finish the job and complete our mission together.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Often in jurisdictions where COVID-19 may be very prevalent and even with the best protective measures, they may come face-to-face with a COVID-19-infected person during their overseas duties.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: These include our public officers at overseas missions, whether from MFA, MTI or MINDEF.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Another related group would be our national sports women and sportsmen, some of whom may be training overseas, some of whom may be back home in Singapore right now, like one of my residents, but at the same time worried about what will happen when they return overseas for studies, when they go overseas to train, and may again come face-to-face with a COVID-19-infected person while flying Singapore's flag.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, I would like to ask the Ministers what is the policy approach that will be taken to support Singapore Public Service officers and our Singaporean sportswomen and sportsmen who represent us overseas, often in jurisdictions where COVID-19 is running rampant?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, these are issues that the Multi-Ministry Taskforce is discussing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also consulting the expert committee on vaccination on how to deal with the various priorities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, our priority is to first protect the healthcare workers, ensure they can continue to preserve our healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, this is the second group that we will be focusing on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are protecting Singapore's interests and we should find ways to protect them as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, all these are factors that will be taken into consideration.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But as the Member pointed out, there are many groups and many of them are also facing challenges.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If it is your turn, please come forward and get vaccinated, do not wait.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is the only way for us to protect individuals as well as to protect one another.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I take the Member's point that there will be different groups that have an interest and that require protection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will see how we can manage our vaccination programme to meet their needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But bearing in mind that the priority is still to protect our healthcare system, our healthcare workers and the next priority are the seniors, who are vulnerable to severe outcomes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: When we first saw the first shipment of the vaccine that arrived in Singapore with Minister Ong receiving at the airport, we were very happy.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: But, subsequently, we were a little bit disappointed with the speed of the roll-out of the vaccine.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: In fact, in Canada, during the Christmas period, they closed the vaccination centre and they were being slammed, "Why did you close the vaccination centres during Christmas?" They should be speeding on now to quickly vaccinate as many people as possible.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Initially, I was hoping that Singapore should be the first country in the world to get the whole country vaccinated.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If any country can do it, Singapore can do it.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Because we are small, we are fast, we are efficient, we are organised.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If this is a war, I would say that vaccination, initially, I was hoping it would be made mandatory.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Of course, the Government has chosen to make it voluntary.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I know that vaccination is a personal choice, but it has public consequences.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I certainly urge everyone to be vaccinated as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: So, I hope that the Ministers now can consider rolling out this vaccination programme faster than what we are talking now.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Because as it is now, I am not sure what are we waiting for.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Next, I would also like to ask when will the Speaker, Deputy Speakers and the Members of Parliament be vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, let me thank Dr Lim Wee Kiak for his enthusiasm and his strong support for our vaccination programme.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our objective is to roll out our vaccination programme as quickly as possible, but we have to bear in mind that we have limited supplies, we need to progress based on the supplies that we can receive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The key reason for our approach is to adopt a cautious one because vaccination is a very complex process, particularly bearing in mind that we need to ensure the ultra cold-chain is intact to ensure the quality and efficacy of the vaccine will not be affected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Next, we also want to make sure the safety of those who are receiving the vaccination, making sure that there is a proper queuing system, they are registered properly, and data are captured accurately.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And we will be rolling out full-scale vaccination for the healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Hopefully, soon we will be able to make it available to Speaker as well as Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is important that we also roll out for the rest of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I agree with Dr Lim and I am equally anxious to cover as many Singaporeans as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I look forward to Members to help support our effort and to convince your constituents to step forward when their turn comes for the vaccination.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two clarifications for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first is whether the Health Sciences Authority or HSA works with any threshold for efficacy before it approves any vaccine.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I read, for example, that in the US, the regulators need a minimum efficacy threshold of about 50%.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does HSA have some minimum threshold that it works with before considering approving any vaccine?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification concerns HSA's approval of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: HSA has announced that it is actually an interim authorisation and that further data – probably longer term data – will need to be submitted by the manufacturer before the vaccine can be given full registration.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like the Minister for Health – for public consumption – to explain what additional information the manufacturer needs to submit in order to get full registration for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I think that the efficacy threshold has to take into account the potential risk that the vaccine may create, the potential risk of adverse incidents, as well as other factors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not a clear-cut threshold that once it is 50.1%, we will approve it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If there is greater uncertainty, then we will require a higher level of efficacy for us to be assured of the benefits versus the risks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also have to take into account the current situation of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If it is a very severe pandemic, then it is important for us to ensure that we vaccinate our population as quickly as possible and, therefore, we may have to accept a lower threshold of efficacy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the pandemic is less severe – low mortality and so on, we may require a higher level of efficacy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Basically, it is a balance of benefits and risks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is a holistic assessment that HSA's experts will have to take into account in coming to a conclusion whether or not it will be approved for use.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because this vaccine has been made available only in recent months and it has only been applied for a couple of months, we still need to monitor how it is applied in real life.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Manufacturers are required to report any adverse incidents that happen so that we can keep track of the performance of the vaccine on the ground as well as the potential risks that it may carry.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: First, we take comfort from Minister Gan's report that Singapore has secured sufficient supplies for the entire Singapore local population and that vaccination is anticipated to complete by the third quarter of 2021.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The second supplementary question is, testing has been a key requirement for travel under COVID-19 conditions.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Particularly, also related to this question on vaccination, how would vaccination be featured in the upcoming World Economic Forum (WEF) to be hosted in Singapore in May?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the delivery of our advance order for vaccines – there is always a risk of non-delivery or a delay in delivery.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we are in close contact with our manufacturers that we have entered into contract with and we are monitoring their delivery schedule, and if our vaccination programme has to be adjusted.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This way, we ensure that we have adequate vaccine supplies for the whole of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With regard to the questions on travel, I will leave them to my Co-Chair to respond.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is just part of that overall system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We know when you get vaccinated, you are protecting yourself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You do not know how much you can protect others.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if the results indicate that vaccinations do offer protection to others, then, clearly, we can make some adjustments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What are some of the adjustments that are possible?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, if there is a concert being held today, typically, under today's rules, we would require a pre-event test for everyone going to the concert.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Subsequently, if we have, again, more evidence, we might say, for travellers, well, you do not need a vaccination to travel but, if you are vaccinated, you travel and you come back, I might consider the extent to which I impose the Stay-Home Notice (SHN) conditions or the number of tests you are required to take.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, those are the things that we are looking at and these are all being studied very carefully For purposes of the WEF event which Ms Foo highlighted, well, if the travellers come in on a vaccine and if we have the data and evidence, then, indeed, we can review the requirements that we impose on these travellers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Otherwise, the basic arrangements for the WEF event will be through existing prevailing measures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, we will bubble wrap a facility.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will put the travellers under frequent testing to ensure that they are safe.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will have safe management measures in place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of these measures are still effective and we should still continue to rely on them.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As alluded to by Dr Lim Wee Kiak as well as Ms Foo Mee Har, I think you will also give Singaporeans comfort to know of the expected delivery timeline of when they will be able to be vaccinated in the rest of the year.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second question is also a follow-up question to what the Minister has said in terms of individual autonomy to choose the vaccines.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For people who are within the same category, for example, who are Singaporeans, who are male and of a certain age, what is the approach or process by which the vaccine is being administered, given that should there be more than one that has been approved?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Would the Ministry provide the up-to-date information as to the different side effects, efficacy rates as well as various clinical trial data for people who are being administered a particular vaccine to have a sense of these are?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Today, we have approved the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine and we are continuing to evaluate two other vaccines that I have mentioned in my speech.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With regard to the second question, I am not quite sure what the question was about.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: How do we administer the vaccine if there are different types?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I have mentioned, it will be based on the assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If there are significant contra-indications for a specific vaccine that, say, for example, is not suitable for young children and another vaccine is suitable, then we will use the vaccine that is suitable for young children, depending on the indication that is provided by the manufacturer.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But if the indications are similar, then it will also depend on the availability of the vaccines at the point in time, whichever stock is available.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So long as we are able to administer them, we would use the vaccine that is available to us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The key is that whatever the source of the vaccine, all of them must meet our safety efficacy requirements.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: From a safety and efficacy point of view, they should be treated similarly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, as the Member has pointed out, we do provide information on these vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think HSA's assessments are published, reports are available and the manufacturers also shared a lot of details with regard to the potential side effects of these vaccines and I have mentioned some of the side effects in my Statement earlier.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One is: this figure of 60% "satisfactory" to the Multi-Ministry Taskforce (MTF), should it be higher, because we had mentioned that we should be looking at above 70% vaccination rate?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Second question is: as more vaccines come on stream or are approved for use in Singapore, the sentiments with regard to different vaccines – will that also be similarly surveyed?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Thirdly, on when these additional vaccines come on stream.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Anecdotally, over the weekend, as I was speaking to residents as well as family members, quite a number of older Singaporeans seemed to indicate a preference for CoronaVac, which is the vaccine that is developed by Sinovac, which is not using the new technology.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For some reason, they indicated that it is because it is older technology, it is more established.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If it comes on stream, they would like to choose to have that.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If, in the event that, at the time that they are assigned to take their vaccinations and these other variants of vaccines are not available and they reject the current vaccines, how soon, when new vaccines come on stream, will they be eligible to be vaccinated?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, regardless of whether it is 60% or 70%, we must work hard to try to get the last person to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We need everyone to chip in to help – the professionals counselling your patients and their family members to get vaccinated and Members of Parliament going down to the ground, persuading their constituents to step forward and get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think we want to push the coverage to as high as possible a level, so that we provide protection especially for those who cannot be vaccinated because of medical conditions and/or for various reasons; and there are some for whom the vaccine may not be effective because effectiveness is 95% for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we need to protect them by making sure that all of us are vaccinated to the extent possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I urge Members to continue to help us to share this message that we want to encourage Singaporeans to step forward to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because until we have the full information, until we have completed the review, I cannot assure you that these vaccines will be available in the short term or even in the long term.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, let us not depend on something that is far away.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When additional vaccines are available, we will share the details with Singaporeans including the safety efficacy data and everything.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We aim to be as transparent as possible, even side effects, adverse events, we share with everyone so that we can all collectively make an informed decision.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think it is important to be transparent, so that we can maintain the trust between the Government and the people and so that we can embark on this vaccination programme together as a country.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong made some comments in respect of the Parliamentary Question I filed for tomorrow's sitting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Essentially, I have asked whether the Government is considering or working on a rechargeable version of the TraceTogether token and whether battery replacement for the current version will be provided without charges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would just like to see some clarification from the Minister following his comments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Does it mean that the Government will provide free replacement of the current token, free replacement with similar models, not a rechargeable version when the battery runs out, say after six months?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I read the literature that the battery will last about six months.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My second clarification is, has the Government already computed at this current non-rechargeable version, if supplied free of charge to all Singaporeans, will cause the Government less in the longer term as compared to a rechargeable version?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And this is not forgetting the environmental costs arising from the current model.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think if you consider the imperatives of what we had to do – roll out the token very quickly and get it distributed in a short time – there is no question, we have to use a version that allows us to use off-the-shelf components.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have to incur more costs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have to incur greater complexity in manufacturing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of it can be done through a simple replacement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Depending on the version of the tokens, because there are different versions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of them can be done just through true a simple replacement of the battery, you need not do a one-for-one swap.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And the Minister's assurance was very helpful in allying their fears.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, let me ask the Minister, what assurances are there that, there would not be adverse side effects which may show up perhaps a few years later, especially for pregnant women.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Another clarification which I wish to ask Minister Lawrence Wong is about the TraceTogether token.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I feel bit disconcerted because I feel that for residents to collect them and keep them as a reserve, is really quite a waste of resources.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And the literature, as the hon Mr Dennis Tan had said, states that the battery runs out in six months and you will be given a free replacement of the battery.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If it is damaged, there will be free replacement of the token.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If you lose it, there will be a first free replacement as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I feel that we should encourage our residents not to waste resources like this.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Use the app if they have it in a smartphone and for those who do not have the smartphone, then yes, we want to encourage them to adopt this TraceTogether programme by collecting the token.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But certainly, for those who have smartphones, I hope that the Minister can reconsider and ask those with smartphones to not collect or not seek a replacement when the battery wears out.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Minister Lawrence Wong can deal with TraceTogether token.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is a safety precaution we are putting in place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are also looking at indications even from a short-term reaction to see whether they are likely to have long-term effects on a pregnancy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are the part of the scientific work that is on-going.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Rest assured that HSA as well as the Expert Committee will take into account all these data before recommending vaccinations for pregnant women.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not see a need to collect my token either because I am quite happy using my app.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to strongly encourage everyone with the app – use the app.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will complete that soon and then, we will transit, as I said, to this new phase of having TraceTogether-only SafeEntry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I share Mr Lim's concerns and I would strongly encourage all of us to put the message out to our residents, the app is just as effective perhaps even more effective when new features are added on, so, please use the app.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To the Minister for Education, I like to clarify that I am not trivialising the effort that the Government has put in from bringing us from Phase Two to Phase Three.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I am also reflecting some sentiments of many Singaporeans that since there is not much change from Phase Two to Phase Three, we would like to know a longer roadmap whereby we will get closer to the pre-COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Although it is a new normal, we would like to see this new normal to be far more liberal than before.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, we would like to know – we would like the Minister to enlighten us on that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some areas that perhaps we would like to ask is that, one, if we attain a certain level of vaccinations, are we going to open up?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Two, if we attain a certain level of testing capability, especially in the rapid test capability, are we going to open up?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Three, can we upgrade further the way we use our tracing technology?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, just now we were talking about the token, why the Government actually introduced token when we could have push everybody into smartphone, in the first place?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, there are all these questions that on the mind of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And to open up, can any of these conditions be satisfied or a combination of these conditions will allow us to be closer to the full opening up?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It would be useful not to repeat some of the questions that have been answered, please.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But in fact, in fact, when you go from five to eight, in groups of five to groups of eight, you are adding a lot of risk.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Particularly, if one person goes out multiple times, each time a group of eight persons eating, dining, visiting, you are adding a lot of risk.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I would say, "Don't sweat the small stuff".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It may appear small but these are significant moves that we are making.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think people do appreciate that they can meet in larger groups, meet with their family members, meet with their loved ones and every time we make one step forward, relax a measure, we are adding risk and all of the risk, do add up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not just simply saying, "The situation looks very good, let's all keep opening up, let's keep opening up." But each time we make a move, we have to be very sure that we have the tools and the enablers to keep the infection under control.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With regard to these different tools on testing, on tracing, we have already reached quite a high level.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have reached the desired capacity of testing that we wanted to build up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is already a very high percentage, probably the highest in the world on a contact tracing system; and we will still try to get a higher rate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, on these, we are doing quite well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have to do this in a controlled manner, recognising that the risks are there and the virus is raging everywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us do this in a very controlled, careful, calibrated manner.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even after we have had a lot of people in Singapore being vaccinated, it does not mean that everything is over.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because no country is safe until everyone in the world is safe and it will take some time for the whole world to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, yes, getting all of us in Singapore vaccinated is important.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will enable us to move further in terms of relaxation of measures for travel, for our own resumption of activities within Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if your hope is to get back to a pre-COVID-19 sort of normal, I think we still have to be circumspect and we still have to be realistic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The virus is still going to be raging in many other parts of the world, vaccinations will take time to distribute to every country, to everyone in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have to be prepared to live with COVID-19 for quite a while.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It has been a long road to get us here and I, for one, feel very thankful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I have two clarification questions that should be very quick to answer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The first is, given that the endorsement for the usage of the vaccine is only for those over 16 and, understanding that, access is voluntary, would it be possible for those under 16, if they wish, to be able to do so, be vaccinated?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The second question is, if I could clarify the definition of residents able to obtain the vaccination, would this generally include LTVP, Employment, Work Pass holders?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think I have answered the question, in order not to waste time for the House.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, if you do take the vaccine, you will be taking a risk.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And I am sure my healthcare professionals would not be in a position to give you a vaccine that has not been authorised for use.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I would say, please, do not get vaccinated if you are below 16.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The trials are on-going, manufacturers are continuing to trial on the people below 16.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When the data is available, and we are able to verify that they are safe and efficacious for those below 16, we would roll it out for those below 16.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think Minister mentioned that they might have to take more thorough tests but I think this was raised to me by a couple of my residents and they said they might choose not to take the vaccination, "Will I be stopped, say, for example, going to watch a movie?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will I be stopped from going to school?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will I be stopped from doing certain things if I do not get vaccinated?" If Minister could, perhaps, clarify this and give the assurance that, perhaps, the Government will not go down this path?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would be useful, I think, for those who do not get vaccinated to know.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are all the prevailing measures that we are used to.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When vaccination comes in, we may relax some of these requirements.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many of us are not vaccinated today except for the healthcare workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we can do many activities subject to prevailing guidelines, prevailing safe distancing measures.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
