text: The idea is that when you get vaccinated, perhaps some of these measures can be relaxed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Exactly what these are, as I said earlier, it is under study and when we have the data, evidence, when we are clear about what changes are possible in our guidelines and measures, we will put that out to the public.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: From MOH's point of view, at the moment, that is not the important question to ask.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The important question, the important issue is to please get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, do not worry too much about what if you are not vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Focus on encouraging your constituents, "Please go ahead and get vaccinated." Reassure them that we have gone through thorough assessment on the safety and efficacy of the vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We encourage all of you to get vaccinated when your turn comes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am concerned about the increase in the imported cases.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I believe he only mentioned Singapore Citizens, PRs and children under six and below?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: On vaccinations, since our vaccine programme has already started with healthcare workers, to give the assurance to everybody, including healthcare workers, that the vaccine is safe, should not our senior public servants, including Ministers, already have been vaccinated by now?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is quite tight and we make sure that these cases, if they were to emerge, are isolated and ring-fenced and do not leak into our local community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There was a second question with regard to our senior public servants and the politicians, whether we should take the lead.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, we will be taking the lead.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As the Prime Minister has said, he will be among the first when his cohort comes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we also do not want to be accused of jumping the queue, that we go ahead of the others.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we have to manage the process to ensure that the first priority is given to the healthcare workers because they are exposed and they are at risk.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Every day, they see the patients and care for the patients, they themselves are exposed to potential infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And therefore, the priority must be given to the healthcare workers first and we are focusing on that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Among the healthcare workers, Prof Leo Yee-Sin who is the CEO of NCID, was among the first batch to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is how she demonstrates her leadership and confidence in the vaccine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think when our turn comes, I am sure all my colleagues would be very happy to step forward to get vaccinated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We have learned quite a lot about new strains or mutations across the globe.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My question is, does this vaccine we have subscribed to anticipate resistance to future strains or are we to get further vaccinations over and above what we have subscribed to?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, is this a moving target, over and above what we are going to get vaccinated for?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to monitor the mutations of the virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think the scientists around the world are watching and monitoring carefully.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned in my speech, mutation happens from time to time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, it happens quite regularly as the virus, basically, is like a photocopying machine so it copies itself and every time it makes copy, it will be slightly different from the version previously.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There will be some specks here and there, some dots here and there that are different.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is possible that one day, the virus may mutate and we may need to modify our vaccine in order to respond to the new virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With the current vaccines that have already been developed, I think it will facilitate the development of the new vaccines if it becomes necessary to respond to new strains of the virus, particularly, with the platform of mRNA, it is much easier for us to replicate, to produce new vaccines in response to variations or mutations in the virus.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just three supplementary questions for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In regard to where the vaccines will be administered, can we take it that they will be administered at polyclinics, public hospitals?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Will every effort be made to ensure that the vaccines can be administered in locations that are close to where people are living in diverse locations across the country?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The second question is, will every effort be made to bring the vaccination process to elderly Singaporeans who are in nursing homes, senior care centres and so on, who may not exactly be very ambulatory?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And, thirdly, just to follow up on the question that my colleague Mr Gerald Giam asked, I do not believe it was answered.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is the Government evaluating the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine as well?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think there are quite a number of vaccines that we are currently evaluating.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would not be at liberty to go into details of which are the vaccines that we are evaluating.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It also depends on the data that we are able to get.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As and when data is made available, publicly or bilaterally from the manufacturer, we review them and we get ourselves updated as much as possible so that when the application is made by the manufacturer for the vaccine to be registered, we will then be ahead of time to be able to make a quick assessment, rather than to start from scratch.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we do this rolling review approach in order for us to speed up the approval process.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I would say that most of the vaccines that are currently being developed, HSA has been keeping a watch on them, and is assessing and reviewing the data as and when they become available.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As and when the vaccine has applied for registration, we will then go into a full swing evaluation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would not be able to share what are the vaccines that have applied, beyond the three that I have mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The other question that where would vaccination sites be, I would say that we will generally take into account accessibility and convenience for those who are receiving the vaccination.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For the healthcare workers, most of them will receive the vaccination within their healthcare institutions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have an existing system to vaccinate their staff and we will tap on those.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will also tap on the polyclinics that are available, operating today, but bearing in mind that the polyclinics also have their usual patients that they need to attend to.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will work with the private clinics as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As you are aware, it requires ultra cold-chain, minus 80 degree Celsius and it needs very careful handling during the administration of the vaccine to the individual.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not so easy to make it available conveniently at all the private clinics.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will need to work with specific clinics and specific chains as well as work with specific, selected vaccination sites so that we are able to construct the infrastructure that is needed for this extra cold-chain storage and administration.
